title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Three things it could find but not cut
summary: Removable unreferenced symbols go from 84 to 95 out of 98 on a real project, and enum entries from 24 to 33 out of 33.

highlights.title: A constructor that wraps is no longer a wall
highlights.description: The header was anchored on the line holding the name, so a data class whose parameters span several lines had no removal at all.

highlights.title: Java fields can be removed
highlights.description: The continuation test listed Kotlin keywords only, and a Java field starts with its type. A trailing semicolon closes the statement in both languages.

highlights.title: One line, two declarations
highlights.description: A whole line extent took the live neighbour with the dead one. No removal invariant counts declarations inside a cut, so nothing reported it.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A declaration whose primary constructor wraps has a removal extent.
A Java field ending on a semicolon has one too.
An enum entry is removable wherever it sits in its list.
A line that carries two declarations yields no removal, so taking the dead one cannot take the live one.
